thread:
laura_sales: Hey team — customer (health-tech) asked for guidance on Private VPC connectivity for their POC. Main asks: preserve client IP, support TLS-inspect middleboxes, SNI rewrite compatibility, and expected egress IPs for allowlisting. Also they want cost implications for PrivateLink vs peering. TL;DR: can we summarize options + short config sample they can hand to their NetOps?

andy_netops: Quick answers up front:
- PrivateLink: traffic stays on AWS control plane -> you hit our endpoint's ENI, source IP usually NATed to endpoint EIP unless you run with proxy that preserves src.
- VPC peering: preserves src IP, simpler for onprem routing but needs route tables + cross-account peering approvals.
- TLS inspect: both work but if you need interception you must terminate TLS at their side or use a trusted proxy; PrivateLink hides SNI sometimes depending on proxy. :eyes:

jun_infra: For POC, recommend 2 options: 1) PrivateLink + reverse proxy in their VPC to preserve client IP in X-Forwarded-For, 2) Peering with Security Group rules and NAT on our side if they can't accept XFF.

maya_sales_eng: Customer also asked about pricing impact — can you list the delta?

andy_netops: Pricing notes: PrivateLink -> hourly interface endpoints + cross-AZ data processing fees (per-GB). Peering -> no endpoint hour fee but inter-AZ / inter-region transfer costs may apply depending on topology. For small POC traffic, PrivateLink is often cheaper to onboard (less infra changes) but sustained heavy traffic can be cheaper on peering.

security_ops: On the security questionnaire part: we need to confirm TLS never terminates on our side for regulated data unless they sign a DPA addendum and we enable dedicated encrypted paths. Also provide them this snippet for FQDN/port allowlist and explain SNI caveat.

laura_sales: Can you paste the allowlist snippet I can send? short and concrete.

andy_netops: Sure — example for onprem firewall / NGFW: 
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood Private endpoint (example)
# Replace <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP> with the egress IP we give the customer
# Replace <REGION> and <SERVICE_FQDN> accordingly
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP> 443
allow udp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_ENDPOINT_EIP> 123  # ntp if required
# If using PrivateLink interface endpoint, allow the AWS-managed ENI CIDRs in the subnet range
```

jun_infra: Also add note: if they rely on TLS inspection, they must allow outbound to service FQDNs so SNI is visible to their proxy (if using SNI-based routing). If their proxy rewrites SNI, that breaks certificate pinning.

maya_sales_eng: What about client IP preservation options (short bullet list I can send)?

andy_netops: Client IP options:
- VPC Peering: native, src IP preserved to our endpoint (recommended if they need src-based ACLs).
- PrivateLink + reverse proxy (recommend NLB + proxy): preserves client in X-Forwarded-For header.
- Using a TCP proxy with proxy protocol v2 to pass original src (we support proxy-protocol at dedicated endpoints).

security_ops: Add: we can support proxy-protocol only on Dedicated & Private deployments (not on the public hosted API).

laura_sales: Great. One blocker: their security team flagged "SNI rewrite could break our mTLS validation" — any mitigation?

jun_infra: Mitigations: terminate mTLS at customer border and use app-level auth to our endpoint, or run a mutual TLS tunnel to a Dedicated instance (we can stand up dedicated endpoint for POC, requires commit).

maya_sales_eng: I'll draft the email with the allowlist + short pros/cons + cost note. Any one-liner we want to add about SLA for PrivateLink vs Peering?

andy_netops: One-liner: "Peering provides simple low-latency path with src-preservation; PrivateLink provides easier onboarding and isolation but may NAT source IPs and incur per-endpoint costs."

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: privatelink-runbook v1.4 published -> https://redwood.example.com/docs/privatelink-handbook :thumbsup:

laura_sales: Perfect. I'll ping once I have the customer's netops contact and the SOC questionnaire entries. Thanks all :raised_hands:
